newsitem.title: USA: TRW sells consumer credit info unit for $1 billion.
newsitem.headline: TRW sells consumer credit info unit for $1 billion.

text.p: TRW Inc. said Thursday it sold its information services business, which operates one of the nation's largest consumer credit report services, to an investor group led by Bain Capital Inc. for $1.01 billion.
TRW will retain a 16 percent stake in the business, which will be named Experian Corp.

"The sale of information services allows the company to sharpen the focus on its core automotive and space and defence businesses," said Joseph T. Gorman, chairman and chief executive officer. "The prospects for growth in both of these markets are excellent.

TRW said previously that proceeds from the sale will be used to fund investment opportunities in the automotive and space and defence industries and purchases under the company's ongoing share buyback programme.
TRW said it expects to take restructuring and other charges that would offset the gain realised by the unit's sale, but did not specify the amount.
TRW is considering steps to enhance its competitiveness in key global markets, provide resources for growth, and increase shareholder value, it said.
Cleveland-based TRW had 1995 sales of about $10 billion.
Its stock rose 62.5 cents to $97.875 on the New York Stock Exchange.
